findings.claim: customManagers[0] regex will not match the current wrapper file because `(?<currentValue>v?[0-9][^\s]*)` requires the `# tag:` comment to start with `v` or a digit, but the actual value is `post-v1.0.0 + warn-msg fix (020D1.1)` which starts with `p`. The overall matchStrings pattern therefore produces zero dependency matches and AC (ii) is unmet.
findings.evidence: renovate/default.json line 38: `(?<currentValue>v?[0-9][^\s]*)`. policy-check-wrapper.yml line 47: `uses: jrnb2024/standards-control-plane/.github/workflows/policy-check.yml@41a529908ef5355b82ca924ef0502fa5ec2fcc11  # tag: post-v1.0.0 + warn-msg fix (020D1.1)`. The `currentValue` capture group requires its first character to satisfy `v?[0-9]`: either a literal `v` or a digit 0-9. The actual first character is `p` (from `post-`). The entire matchStrings[0] pattern fails; Renovate sees 0 dependencies from this customManager on the current file.
findings.impact: Renovate's customManager is silently non-functional against the current policy-check-wrapper.yml. No bump PRs will be generated when SCP cuts future release tags. The self-dogfood cascade loop — the primary purpose of 020F — does not operate. DISPATCH-NOTE.md AC (ii) ('regex bumps SHA + tag-comment atomically') is unmet.
findings.mitigation: After 020H part 2 promotes v1.0.0, update the `# tag:` comment in policy-check-wrapper.yml to the real semver tag: `# tag: v1.0.0`. The regex will then match. Do not broaden the `currentValue` pattern without also replacing `versioningTemplate: semver` — widening the regex alone does not fix COR-002. Both COR-001 and COR-002 share one root fix: a real semver value in the tag comment.

findings.claim: Even if the `currentValue` capture group were broadened to accept `post-v1.0.0 + warn-msg fix (020D1.1)`, `versioningTemplate: "semver"` in customManagers[0] would refuse to parse it as semver and Renovate would skip or error on the dependency. This is a second, independent failure mode layered on COR-001.
findings.evidence: renovate/default.json line 43: `"versioningTemplate": "semver"`. Renovate's semver versioning requires `currentValue` to be a parseable semver string (optionally v-prefixed per node-semver). `post-v1.0.0 + warn-msg fix (020D1.1)` is not parseable as semver under any semver spec variant. Even if a looser regex captured the raw string, Renovate would log a 'not a valid semver' warning and produce no bump PR.
findings.impact: The regex fix (COR-001) is necessary but not sufficient. Without a real semver currentValue, `versioningTemplate: semver` causes a second failure. The result is identical: no bump PRs.
findings.mitigation: Shared root fix with COR-001: update the `# tag:` comment to `v1.0.0` after 020H part 2 cuts the tag. No change to `versioningTemplate` is needed once the comment contains a real semver. Acknowledged as an intentional transition-state limitation: the @SHA pin is operationally correct and manually maintained; Renovate automation becomes functional when proper semver tags are in use.

findings.claim: `renovate.json` extends the preset without a tag pin. The extends entry `github>jrnb2024/standards-control-plane//renovate/default` has no `#renovate/v1.0.0` suffix, so any breaking commit to the default branch immediately propagates to SCP's Renovate config on the next scheduled run, with no rollback window.
findings.evidence: renovate.json line 5: `"github>jrnb2024/standards-control-plane//renovate/default"`. DISPATCH-NOTE.md 'Tag series' section documents the `renovate/v*` tag series and states initial publication of `renovate/v1.0.0` happens post-merge — but the consumer does not reference it. Renovate resolves untagged preset references to the repository's default branch HEAD at evaluation time.
findings.impact: A broken preset commit on main propagates to SCP's own Renovate config without the author having to bump a version. For a self-consuming preset this is scope-contained to SCP only, but it is inconsistent with the stated `renovate/v*` tag-series design intent. If the preset author introduces a misconfiguration mid-week, all Renovate runs between that commit and detection inherit it.
findings.mitigation: After cutting `renovate/v1.0.0` (DISPATCH-NOTE post-merge step), update `renovate.json` to `"github>jrnb2024/standards-control-plane//renovate/default#renovate/v1.0.0"`. Track as a follow-up to 020F. Transition-state acceptable since SCP is the sole preset author.

findings.claim: `prBodyNotes` URL template `v{{newValue}}` may produce a double `v` prefix (e.g., `vv1.0.0`) if Renovate passes GitHub tag names as-is in `{{newValue}}` when the tags are named `v1.0.0`.
findings.evidence: renovate/default.json line 26: `https://github.com/jrnb2024/standards-control-plane/releases/tag/v{{newValue}}`. With `github-tags` datasource and `semver` versioning, Renovate's behaviour for `{{newValue}}` depends on whether it strips the `v` prefix before templating. If tags are named `v1.0.0` and Renovate exposes `newValue = v1.0.0` (tag name as-is), the URL becomes `/releases/tag/vv1.0.0` (broken link). Renovate typically normalises to strip the `v` prefix in semver mode, yielding `newValue = 1.0.0` and a correct URL — but this is version-dependent behaviour.
findings.impact: Broken release-notes URL in PR body text only. No functional or security impact. Affects reviewer UX when inspecting bump PRs.
findings.mitigation: Prefer `{{newValue}}` alone (no leading `v`) and verify the URL after the first real bump PR is generated. If the tag name includes `v`, Renovate's `{{newValue}}` already contains it.

structured_review.summary: Two MAJ findings block AC (ii): the customManagers[0] regex will not match the current wrapper's `# tag: post-v1.0.0 + warn-msg fix (020D1.1)` comment value (fails `v?[0-9]` first-character requirement), and `versioningTemplate: semver` would independently reject the same string even if captured. Both are resolved by a single root fix: update the `# tag:` comment in policy-check-wrapper.yml to a real semver value (`v1.0.0`) after 020H part 2 cuts the release tag. One MIN (preset consumer lacks a tag pin, inconsistent with the renovate/v* tag-series design) and one nit (potential double-v in PR body URL). Verdict: FAIL on AC (ii); ACs (i)(iii)(iv)(v) pass; AC (vi) passes with notes; AC (vii) out of scope.
